en: The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Vajra Life-Span of All Tathāgatas Spoken by the Buddha.
[Recorded by] Suo Guo... [Title omitted for brevity].

The Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery—honored with a fief of three thousand households, invested with the purple robe, posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works, and bestowed the honorific name Dajian (Great Mirror)—translated this by imperial decree. Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying on the banks of the Gaṅgā River,
together with a great assembly of bhikṣus, bodhisattvas, and immeasurable multitudes of devas and humans.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Four Heavenly Kings, Vaiśravaṇa and the others, saying:
There are four kinds of phenomena that are truly terrifying;
whether male or female, boy or girl,
there is no sentient being whatsoever who can escape them.
Regarding what are called birth, old age, sickness,
and death, among them one phenomenon is the most pervasive affliction and is most difficult to remedy.
Regarding what is called the fear of death,
out of compassion for them, I have taught the Dharma as an antidote.
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One, today I have attained great benefit.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will, for the sake of all sentient beings, proclaim this Dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One turned his face toward the east.
With a snap of the fingers, he summoned all the Tathāgatas and made this vow:
"All you Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the ten directions..."
For the sake of all sentient beings,
may those who have realized bodhi all assist me,
so that by means of the majestic spiritual power of all Tathāgatas, I may [accomplish this].
I cause all sentient beings to transform their non-life-sustaining karma and increase their lifespan. In the past,
before I was for the sake of sentient beings, I had not yet turned this wheel of Dharma.
Now it is being turned;
it can cause sentient beings to fully achieve longevity, physical form, and strength, so that they are free from the fear of untimely death.
Thus it is in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below.
The summons and the proclamation were likewise made.
At that time, all Tathāgatas from as many worlds as could be reached by the Buddha-eye throughout the ten directions assembled together.
Pervading the entirety of space, as numerous as motes of dust,
at that time all the Buddhas, for the sake of bestowing their empowerment,
spoke with one voice in unison:
Then he spoke the Vajrāyus-dhāraṇī of all Tathāgatas, which says: *tadyathā | tra le tra le minadhi sarvasatvānām kṣāraṅgarṇaṃ praśamantu*.
Sarvaloke (6) sarvasattvānām (7) ānaye (8) kunaye (9) care care (10) hime hauri (11) himeni campini (12) himaśikhi (13) kārave (14) kārame (15) he.
16. Kru-mi | 17. Śrī-pam | 18. Kuma-ti | 19. Viśamani | 20. Śu-śu-viva | 21. A-jhali | 22. Mi-jhali | 23.
Ma-vilam-ma | 24. Hu-mau hu-mau | 25. Oṃ | 26. Mañjaraḥ |
Addressing the Master [Name], twenty-six times *svāhā*.
At that time, at the abodes of the Buddhas of the ten directions, all the Vajradhara Bodhisattvas, with one voice and in unison, also spoke this longevity-extending dhāraṇī, saying:
HŪṂ HŪṂ ŚIKHI SVĀHĀ. After all these Tathāgatas and the Vajradhara Bodhisattvas of the ten directions had spoken this dhāraṇī, they vanished and did not appear again.
At that time, the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa addressed the Buddha,
saying: "I too, by means of the Buddha's spiritual power,
shall provide empowerment, protection, and mindfulness for all sentient beings."
Except for the sake of life, I shall recite the dhāraṇī:
*Sviti* (svasti), *Svit-tar-i*, *Riri*. At that time, the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka again addressed the Buddha, saying:
I too, by the spiritual power of the Buddha,
shall preach a dhāraṇī for the sake of removing untimely death for many sentient beings.
1. Maṇḍanī, 2. Maṇḍanī, 3. Śūma śūma mo. At that time, the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra also addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I, too, for the sake of all sentient beings..."
"The dhāraṇī is taught for the purpose of removing the fear of death.
*Cche-ta-tse cche-ta-tse* (1) *tse-la-ch'ing*. At that time, the Deva King Virūpākṣa also addressed the Buddha, saying:
I, too, by the spiritual power of the Buddha, shall cause all sentient beings to abandon the taking of life and shall preach this dhāraṇī.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Four Heavenly Kings, saying: "Mama māma māma."
If there are those who read and recite this sutra,
upholding it even once every day,
one should revere those good men and good women.
One should regard this as being like the Buddha; one will certainly not fall into the three evil realms and will surely increase one's lifespan.
If a person recites and reads this sutra every day for the sake of all sentient beings, [the same result shall be attained].
In the end, there will be no fear of premature death or a short lifespan,
nor will there be evil dreams, malevolent spirits,
curses, or hideous forms.
They will not be terrified by rākṣasas or malevolent spirits,
nor will they be harmed by water, fire, weapons, or poisons.
All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas will embrace and protect that place.
They shall also be protected and sustained by the Buddha.
At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished preaching this sutra,
the Great King Vaiśravaṇa and the entire great assembly—
All were greatly rejoiced, believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
Thus concludes the *Buddha-spoken Sūtra of the Vajra Life Span Dhāraṇī of All Tathāgatas*.
